# The Peace Only Christ Can Give

## Scripture

“Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you. Not as the world gives do I give to you. Let not your hearts be troubled, neither let them be afraid.” — John 14:27

## Reflection

Jesus spoke these words on the night He was betrayed—hours before arrest, trial, and the cross. He did not promise the absence of trouble but a peace that could coexist with it. The world’s peace depends on circumstances cooperating; Christ’s peace rests on His presence and His finished work. That distinction matters when the news is bad, the body is weak, or the future is uncertain.

Notice the grammar: peace is *given*, not achieved. We do not manufacture calm through sheer willpower or positive thinking. We receive it, the way we receive forgiveness—by faith, not by striving. And notice the command that follows: “Let not your hearts be troubled.” This is not a rebuke of grief but an invitation to direct our anxious thoughts toward the One who holds all things.

Practically, this means we can bring our fears into the light rather than rehearsing them in the dark. When anxiety rises, name it honestly before God, then recall one specific promise from His Word. Peace often grows through small, repeated acts of trust—a prayer whispered at midnight, a verse taped to the mirror, a phone call to a believing friend. The peace of Christ is not fragile. It guards the heart that keeps returning to Him.

## Prayer

Father, we thank You for the peace Christ gives—not dependent on our circumstances but on Your faithfulness. Quiet our anxious hearts today. Help us receive Your peace by faith and rest in Your presence. In Jesus’ name, amen.

## One-Line Application

When anxiety rises, name it to God and rest in one specific promise.
